model.distribution: independent mean-one lognormal multiplicative errors with common log standard deviation sigma on every nonzero L ratio and D capacitor
model.calibration: least-squares removal of one positive global capacitance scale
model.metric: relative spectral-norm error of the calibrated inverse capacitance matrix

designDecision.modelBasedQualificationTarget: sigma at or below 0.002 gives an observed 99.98 percent pass fraction and a 95 percent Wilson lower bound above 99.88 percent
designDecision.warningBand: sigma 0.003 gives 96.12 percent observed yield and p95 inverse error 0.967 percent, leaving little unmodelled margin
designDecision.transition: sigma 0.005 gives 47.62 percent observed yield and median inverse error 1.016 percent
designDecision.commissioningRule: use sigma 0.002 only as an iid component-procurement prior; acceptance still requires direct full-matrix measurement and covariance propagation on every realized device
designDecision.supersededBy: leech-transformer-correlated-tolerance-v1 revises the cross-model procurement target to sigma 0.0015

epistemicStatus.theorem: for every sampled positive D and unit-lower-triangular L, the synthesized capacitance matrix remains positive definite
epistemicStatus.conditionalInference: the recorded yields estimate performance only under the declared independent lognormal component model and calibration rule
epistemicStatus.notEstablished: real fabrication errors are independent, lognormal, stationary or fully represented by the 276 modeled parameters

established: under the declared structured-error model, the selected exact factor tolerates roughly 0.2 percent component log scatter at greater than 99 percent model yield, while the yield transition occurs near 0.5 percent
boundary: Monte Carlo yield is conditional engineering evidence, not a theorem about hardware. Correlated gradients, parasitic modes, frequency dependence, loss, drift, nonreciprocity and readout covariance are absent and must be measured before Gate A promotion.
